summary_html: Federal transparency statutes—**FOIA** and **Sunshine Act**—require disclosure of government data. Project Milk Carton promotes FOIA requests and public dashboards for child-welfare records.
authority_html:
- **Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552)** — public access to records  
- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Matter of New York Civ. Liberties Union v. City of Rochester
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals affirmed, holding that FOIL's personal privacy exemption does not permit an agency to withhold categorically all disciplinary records relating to unsubstantiated complaints; the agency must review each record individually and articulate a particularized and specific justification, disclosing with redactions where redaction would prevent an unwarranted invasion of privacy.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Court of Appeals' current statement of the record-by-record, particularized-justification rule governing FOIL requests to New York agencies.
key_cases.quote: Public Officers Law § 87 (2) requires an agency to evaluate each record individually and determine whether "a particularized and specific justification" exists for denying access

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Lee TT. v. Dowling
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals held that the 'some credible evidence' standard for retaining an indicated report in the Statewide Central Register violates federal due process to the extent the report is disseminated to provider and licensing agencies, and that a subject is entitled to a pre-deprivation hearing at which the agency must prove the abuse or maltreatment by a fair preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion delineates the confidentiality and controlled-disclosure regime governing child-abuse records in New York.
key_cases.quote: subjects are entitled to a predeprivation hearing to determine by a fair preponderance of the evidence whether reports of abuse can be substantiated and relevant to future employment or licensure

key_cases.case_name: Matter of Lawyers for Children v. New York State Office of Children & Family Services
key_cases.citation: 2025 NY Slip Op 02115 (N.Y. App. Div. 3d Dep't Apr. 10, 2025)
key_cases.court: Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of the State of New York, Third Department
key_cases.holding: Over a dissent, the Third Department affirmed dismissal of an article 78 challenge to OCFS's Host Family Home regulations, holding that OCFS did not exceed its authority because the program is a preventive service in which the parent, not the State, decides whether and with whom to place the child.
key_cases.quote: Petitioners' argument that OCFS exceeded its authority when it created the Host Family Home program is unpersuasive
